raw:
At supper, the long table is less formal than it was on your first night. A bowl of roasted onions steams beside the bread, and someone has left the salt cellar within Ashara’s reach, which appears to be a considered precaution.

You take an open chair midway down the table. Seraphel sits across from you, a narrow booklet of choir music tucked beside her plate. She is not in conversation; Aldric is reading a notice beside her with the intense concentration of someone who may be avoiding looking up.

You ask whether she knows a song worth learning.

Seraphel’s smile appears.

“Try *Lantern Road.* Its chorus isn’t long;  
It suits a small room better than a difficult song.  
I like it because each shore adds something more;  
No one sings it quite the way they did before.”

“The mountain version replaces the lamps with stars,” Ysolde says. “It is more accurate.”

Caelindra looks up from her dinner. “It also has a fifth verse no one needs.”

Seraphel inclines her head.

“The fifth verse gets omitted, that much is true;  
It has too many verses for a meal with stew.  
If you would like, I’ll sing the first verse through,  
Or lend you a written copy after supper, too?”
